questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Speaking disrespectfully about sacred or religious things.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Speaking disrespectfully about sacred or religious things.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The word "Blasphemy" means speaking disrespectfully about sacred or religious things. (ईशनिंदा)
    • Example: His speech was considered blasphemy by the religious community.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Mystic (रहस्यवादी): Someone who seeks, through contemplation and self-surrender, to obtain unity with or absorption into the Deity or the absolute, or who believes in the spiritual apprehension of truths that are beyond the intellect.
    • Example: The mystic spent years meditating in the mountains, seeking enlightenment.
  • Atheist (नास्तिक): A person who disbelieves or lacks belief in the existence of God or gods.
    • Example: The atheist challenged the religious doctrines during the debate.
  • Theist (आस्तिक): A person who believes in the existence of a god or gods, specifically of a creator who intervenes in the universe.
    • Example: The theist regularly attended church services and believed in divine intervention.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Adequate
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Adequate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Sufficient.

Key Points

  • The word "adequate" means enough or satisfactory for a particular purpose. (पर्याप्त)
    • Example: The food supply was adequate to meet the needs of the population.
  • "Sufficient" refers to an amount that is enough to meet the needs or purposes. (पर्याप्त)
    • Example: They had sufficient evidence to support their claims.
  • Hence, we can infer that the synonym of 'adequate' is 'sufficient'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Sufficient.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Evaluate (मूल्यांकन करना): To judge or determine the significance, worth, or quality of something.
    • Example: The teacher will evaluate the students' projects next week.
  • Hidden (छिपा हुआ): Not visible or not able to be seen.
    • Example: There was a hidden compartment in the drawer.
  • Reconcile (मेल-मिलाप करना): To restore friendly relations between or to make consistent or congruous.
    • Example: They decided to reconcile their differences and work together.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Brittle
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Brittle
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The word "brittle" means something that is hard but liable to break or shatter easily. (भंगुर)
    • Example: The brittle glass vase broke into pieces when it fell off the table.
  • "Fragile" means something that is easily broken or damaged. (नाज़ुक)
    • Example: Handle the fragile items with care to avoid breaking them.
  • Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate synonym of 'brittle' is 'fragile'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Furtive (चोरी-छिपे): Attempting to avoid notice or attention, typically because of guilt or a belief that discovery would lead to trouble.
    • Example: She cast a furtive glance over her shoulder to make sure no one was following her.
  • Fickle (अस्थिर ): Changing frequently, especially as regards one's loyalties or affections.
    • Example: The weather can be very fickle in this region; it changes from sunny to rainy within minutes.
  • Fatal (घातक): Leading to failure or disaster.
    • Example: The accident proved to be fatal for the driver.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Cherish

  • Hence, we can infer that the synonym of 'cherish' is 'nurture'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Nurture.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Neglect (उपेक्षा): Fail to care for properly.
    • Example: He was accused of neglecting his duties as a parent.

  • Afflict (पीड़ित करना): Cause pain or suffering to; affect or trouble.
    • Example: Many people are afflicted by the common cold during winter.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (O) attitude is (P) or tendency in individuals (Q) a broad-based behaviour (R) which implies (S) a hypothetical postulate
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(O) attitude is
(P) or tendency in individuals
(Q) a broad-based behaviour
(R) which implies
(S) a hypothetical postulate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (2) i.e. OSRQP
Key Points
  • The sentence begins with the subject and main verb "attitude is," which is correctly indicated by part (O). 
  • Following the subject, "a hypothetical postulate" (S) continues the logical sequence, making it clear what attitude is described as.
  • The next part, "which implies" starts the explanation about what the postulate signifies, indicated by (R).
  • The explanation continues with "a broad-based behaviour," indicated by (Q).
  • Ending with "or tendency in individuals" (P) completes the sentence by describing the implications of the behaviour.
Therefore, the correct answer is OSRQP.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (SQPRO): This option starts with "a hypothetical postulate or tendency in individuals," which makes the sentence grammatically incorrect and jumbled.
  • Option 3 (OPQRS): This option starts with "attitude is or tendency in individuals," creating a disjointed and nonsensical sentence.
  • Option 4 (OPSRQ): This option starts with "attitude is or tendency in individuals which implies," which leads to a confusing and grammatically incorrect sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Material
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Material
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points

  • The word "Material" means something that is physical, tangible, and can be perceived by the senses. (भौतिक)
    • Example: The material used in the construction of the building is of high quality.
  • "Abstract" refers to something that exists in thought or as an idea but does not have a physical or concrete existence. (सैद्धांतिक)
    • Example: Her ideas were too abstract to be understood by everyone in the room.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Material' is 'Abstract'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Cheap (सस्ता): Low in price, especially in relation to similar items or services.
    • Example: The cheap shoes wore out quickly after just a few weeks of use.
  • Concrete (ठोस): Existing in a material or physical form; real or solid.
    • Example: They provided concrete evidence to support their claims.
  • Temporary (अस्थायी): Lasting for only a limited period of time; not permanent.
    • Example: The repairs are temporary until a permanent solution can be found.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate homonyms from the given alternatives to fill in the blanks. The rowing instructor commanded them to ________ in a ________. A.row (verb) B.roe C.row (sequence)

B.roe

questions.solution:

Key Points
  • The word "row (verb)" (A) means to propel a boat forward using oars. (पंक्तिबद्ध करना)

questions.question: Identify the error in the following sentence. Ourselves should not boast of one's knowledge.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the error in the following sentence.
Ourselves should not boast of one's knowledge.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect reflexive pronoun "Ourselves."
  • The appropriate pronoun should be "One" to match the possessive pronoun "one's."
  • Proper pronoun agreement ensures grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in Option 3 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "One should not boast of one's knowledge."
 
Additional Information

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Off and on

Off and on

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe. B. The country has 100 major oil and gas fields. C. The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum. D. The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.
A. These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe.
B. The country has 100 major oil and gas fields.
C. The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum.
D. The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (3) i.e. CBAD
Key Points
  • The sequence begins with the introduction of the main topic, "The economy of Saudi Arabia is based on petroleum," which is correctly indicated by part (C). 
  • Following the introduction, "The country has 100 major oil and gas fields" provides further detail about the petroleum economy, indicated by (B).
  • The next part, "These are responsible for producing the major fuel used across the globe," connects to the previous sentence by referring to the oil and gas fields, indicated by (A).
  • The final part, "The chief oil field is Ghawar Field having an estimated 70 billion reserve resource," gives a specific example of one of these fields, indicated by (D).
Therefore, the correct answer is CBAD.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (DCAB): This arrangement starts with the specific detail of Ghawar Field, making it less logical as an introduction to the topic.
  • Option 2 (ABCD): This starts with the fields' responsibility for fuel production without introducing the context, making it less coherent.
  • Option 4 (BACD): This incorrect sequence places the main introduction (C) after details about the fields, disrupting the logical flow.

Key Points

  • The word "restraunt" is a misspelling of "restaurant" which means a place where people pay to sit and eat meals that are cooked and served on the premises. (रेस्टोरेंट)
    • Example: The restaurant was known for its excellent seafood.
  • The word "beleive" is a misspelling of "believe" which means to accept something as true or to have faith in something. (विश्वास करना)
    • Example: I can't believe it's already the end of the year.
  • The word "assigment" is a misspelling of "assignment" which means a task or piece of work allocated to someone as part of a job or course of study. (असाइनमेंट)
    • Example: The students submitted their assignments on time.
  • The word "embarassed" is a misspelling of "embarrassed" which means feeling or showing embarrassment. (शर्मिंदा)
    • Example: She felt embarrassed when she realized her mistake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Delicious (स्वादिष्ट): Highly pleasant to the taste.
    • Example: The cake was absolutely delicious.
  • Silly (मूर्खतापूर्ण): Lacking in good sense or judgment.
    • Example: It was a silly mistake to forget the keys.
  • Colleague (सहकर्मी): A person with whom one works in a profession or business.
    • Example: She always gets along well with her colleagues.
  • Utterly (पूरी तरह से): Completely and without qualification.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, chiefly because of a boost in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, chiefly because of a boost in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients.

options.text: pretty much entirely because of a boil-down
options.html: pretty much entirely because of a boil-down

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "chiefly because of a boost" needs a more precise and formal substitute suitable for the context.
  • "Owing primarily to a rise" is a more formal and contextually appropriate option for explaining the growth in the industry.
  • "Owing primarily to" replaces "chiefly because of," and "a rise" replaces "a boost," which fits better in this context.
Therefore, the corrected sentence should be "The food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, owing primarily to a rise in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients."
 
Correct Sentence: "The food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, owing primarily to a rise in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "contextually because of a spark" – The phrase "contextually because of a spark" is not appropriate in this formal context.
  • Option 2: "pretty much entirely because of a boil-down" – This phrase is too informal and inappropriate for the context of explaining industry growth.
  • Option 3: "casually due to a growth" – The adverb "casually" is not suitable for this formal context.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The teenager delivered the speech.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The teenager delivered the speech.

options.text: The speech has been delivered by the teenager.
options.html: The speech has been delivered by the teenager.

options.text: The speech is delivered by the teenager.
options.html: The speech is delivered by the teenager.

options.text: The speech was delivered by the teenager.
options.html: The speech was delivered by the teenager.

options.text: The speech was being delivered by the teenager.
options.html: The speech was being delivered by the teenager.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "The teenager delivered the speech."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the speech" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "delivered" to "was delivered" (past simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the teenager."
  • Ensure the sentence remains clear and retains its original meaning.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "The speech was delivered by the teenager."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "The speech has been delivered by the teenager." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
  • Option 2: "The speech is delivered by the teenager." – Incorrect tense (present simple passive).
  • Option 4: "The speech was being delivered by the teenager." – Incorrect aspect (past continuous passive).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold. The city has immense coal piers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'creating'.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence uses parallel structure, listing actions related to culture: creating, understanding, and protecting.
  • 'Creating' is the gerund form that fits the syntax and maintains the parallel structure with 'understanding' and 'protecting.'
  • Other options like 'creation,' 'to create,' and 'create' do not grammatically align with the rest of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.
 
Additional Information
  • Creation (सृजन): A noun, grammatical mismatch.
  • To create (बनाने के लिए): Infinitive verb form, grammatically incorrect in context.
  • Create (बनाना): Simple present form, doesn't fit with parallel structure.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'are'.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence lists multiple activities (understanding, taking care, providing nourishment) which together form a compound subject.
  • The use of "are" is appropriate because these activities collectively require a plural verb form.
  • Other options "is," "were," and "was" do not fit the grammar and context of this compound subject.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.
